context: Animated bar chart race showing World GDP rankings for 15 countries from 1993–2023, displaying the top 12 at any given time with play/pause controls, speed multipliers, and a scrubber for manual seeking.
first_impression: Clean and readable at a glance — well-spaced bars, clear country labels, and a large year watermark anchor the viewer in time.
what_works: Redundant encoding (country name left of bar + 2-letter code inside bar) removes reliance on color alone for identification, substantially mitigating the 15-color overload risk. Speed controls and a scrubber give the viewer genuine agency over pacing.
what_doesnt: The 15-color palette combines Tol Bright and Tol Muted sets that include perceptually similar hues (e.g. #EE6677 and #CC6677 are near-identical reds), which could cause confusion if labels are ever occluded. Animation smoothness and object constancy during rank changes — the core perceptual challenge of bar chart races — cannot be assessed from a static screenshot; the linear-eased, sub-year interpolation approach is architecturally sound but real-motion evaluation is needed.
